analytic_obligations.check: The subsection explicitly replaces the standing compact space by its local affine surface and returns to the standing setting afterward.
The quotient map satisfies z1z2=z3 squared, is finite of degree two, and is unramified off the vertex.
The even-total invariant convergent series split into F0(s squared,t squared)+st F1(s squared,t squared), proving analytic descent at the vertex.
The two canonical-form charts cover the smooth locus and agree by differentiating the defining equation.
Both pullback canonical forms equal2 ds wedge dt and are nonvanishing off the vertex.
The hypersurface residue gives the dualizing generator; div(z1)=2E and4D=2E give the stated fourth-power boundary generator.
The fourth root of the squared boundary tensor pulls back to a constant times absolute s to the minus1 times area product.
The zero-boundary volume pulls back to a positive constant times area product.
A change of local generator by a holomorphic unit changes integrability only by bounded positive factors on smaller neighborhoods.
The adapted-volume ideal is defined by holomorphic germ integrability with the book's e to minus u weight.
Its prescribed volume and boundary are explicitly distinguished from smooth-model resolution-ideal equivalence.
The quadrant lemma requires all five parameters to be strictly positive.
On the first wedge, integrating q produces the coefficient alpha-A+beta A/B; the finite strip is controlled by beta>0.
On the second wedge, integrating p produces beta-B+alpha B/A; its finite strip is controlled by alpha>0.
Both tail coefficients have exactly the sign of alpha/A+beta/B-1; equality gives a divergent constant tail.
The potential is an ambient psh maximum restricted to the quotient surface.
Its two axis restrictions have irrational coefficient ratio, incompatible with a common analytic-singularity coefficient times integer orders.
The finite covering degree changes the integral by a fixed positive factor; bidisk neighborhoods suffice for local finiteness.
The book potential is twice Seo's source potential, preserving source e to minus2phi integrability.
Pullback doubles each squared-log coefficient, giving2sqrt2 and4.
Logarithmic radial coordinates and area Jacobians give alpha=a+1/2,beta=b+1 for D, and alpha=a+1 for zero boundary.
The two strict monomial inequalities therefore follow directly from the independent quadrant lemma.
Separate rotation invariance, angular Parseval and Tonelli give coefficientwise necessity, without cancellation.
Only nonnegative even-total exponents occur for holomorphic germs on the quotient.
For D, all a>=2 terms divide by s squared, all a=1 terms by st, and a=0 even terms pass exactly for b>=4.
The three D minimal exponents each pass the strict criterion; constant and t squared fail.
For zero boundary, precisely the nonconstant even-total terms pass, with minimal exponents(2,0),(1,1),(0,2).
Division of each selected convergent-series group preserves convergence on a smaller bidisk and even-total invariance.
The coefficient germs descend and are bounded on a smaller neighborhood, proving full-series sufficiency from finite generators.
Away from the vertex the potential is bounded, and the only boundary-volume singularity is absolute z3 to the minus1, which is integrable in one complex variable.
Both generated ideals have a unit away from the vertex, proving the claimed global sheaf identities.
Only the explicit quotient example is adopted; no general Newton-body, negative-boundary or fractional-ideal theorem is used.
